label: fed-back first token p (copy step recall_idx 1)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, on the step right after <DEL> where the model gets back its own first output, and only when that token is p (orig(0) = p, recall_idx = 1). It never fires during the original phase, on <DEL>, or on p inputs anywhere else. Magnitude drops as L grows: it is strongest for L = 4-6 (top examples are L = 5, about 2.6-2.8), weaker at L = 7-8, and usually zero at L = 9, which accounts for most false positives (adding L <= 8 raises dev F1 to 0.93). There is a faint residual (0.7% of activation mass) at recall_idx 2 when orig(1) = p is fed back. Magnitude does not depend on the output token or on the other sequence tokens.

issues: The claims hold up. On the dev profile, all activation is in the copy phase (share 1.000), with none on original or <DEL> steps. All of it is on in_tok p (share 1.000). recall_idx 1 holds 0.993 of the activation mass and recall_idx 2 holds 0.007.

The length decay is real and it is where the false positives come from. Restricted to recall_idx 1 with p input, L=9 alone has test precision 0.26. Adding L<=8 raises test precision from 0.862 to 0.984 and F1 from 0.896 to 0.932. The 224 false positives left over are mostly at L=8 near the cutoff, which fits a gradual decay rather than a separate class.

The misses that remain under the L<=8 predicate are all tiny. They hold 1.2% of the activation mass and sit at 0.01-0.12 of max. They are either L=9 recall_idx 1 cases or the faint residual at recall_idx 2 when orig(1)=p. Adding recall_idx 2 to the predicate drops precision to 0.53 (F1 0.68), so leaving it out is correct.

Minor overclaim: the label leaves out the length condition, even though the feature is mostly off at L=9. I did not test the claim that magnitude does not depend on the output token or the other tokens.
